subject: ServiceOps access audit & temporary break-glass request
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@elara.io>, Elara Systems - Ops Team <elara-ops@elara.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ServiceOps access audit & temporary break-glass request

Hi Alex / Elara team,

Thanks for the call this morning — good alignment on the use case. Quick recap and asks so we can move to a mutual action plan (MAP):

Summary of requirements we captured:
- PII types: customer names, email addresses, support transcripts, and payment token partials (no raw CC).
- Retention: you indicated primary retention = 365 days, with a 90-day option for ephemeral logs for session data.
- Logging: full audit trail required for any support/engineer sessions (who, when, actions, and the API call payload hashes).
- Data residency: US-only for production workspace (us-east preferred).
- Support access model: least-privilege RBAC, time-limited break-glass with 4-eyes approval, and session recording/immutable logs for audit.

What we delivered in the call:
- Proposed privilege matrix + initial break-glass flow (attached: privilege_matrix_draft.xlsx).
- Scope doc with proposed retention and logging SLAs (attached: redwood_scope_v1.pdf).

Immediate asks (please reply inline):
1) Confirm US-only residency for production (us-east) or specify other regions.
2) Confirm target retention for session logs (90 / 365 / other).
3) Do you require full verbatim session transcripts for audit, or are hashed-transcript artifacts sufficient?
4) Will you accept JIT (just-in-time) support sessions initiated via our Support Portal with customer approval flow?

Next steps we propose:
- We (Redwood) will update the privilege matrix based on your answers and share a v2 by end of day tomorrow.
- Marissa will schedule a short SSO/SCIM PoC to ensure scoped support accounts are provisioned correctly.
- Hannah (security) is copied to prepare SOC 2 wording and break-glass audit language for the MAP.

Attachments: redwood_scope_v1.pdf (PDF), privilege_matrix_draft.xlsx (Excel).

Thanks — aim to lock these items so we can push the MAP to DocuSign next week.

--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Soto <alex.soto@elara.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elara Systems - Ops Team <elara-ops@elara.io>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 13:05:12 -0400
Subject: Re: ServiceOps access audit & temporary break-glass request

Karthik — thanks for the notes and the attachments. Quick answers below and a couple of follow ups: 

- Residency: Confirm US-only, prefer us-east region for production.
- Retention: We want audit logs retained for 365 days. Session recordings/transcripts: ideally we would have verbatim transcripts for critical sessions for compliance, but if that's not possible hashed transcripts with a replay index could work for now.
- JIT support: yes, JIT via a portal is acceptable but we need the approval to be auditable and trigger a customer alert (email + webhook).

Two clarifying questions: 
1) What level of granularity will you capture in the "action" audit logs? (e.g., full request/response bodies, or action verbs + resource id + hashes)
2) For break-glass approvals, can we require two internal approvers from Elara + automated notification to our security slack channel?

On the MAP timing — we're targeting budget approvals by next Tuesday so a DocuSign by early next week would be great.

On Thu, Jun 10, 2027 at 09:12 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> [Quoted call recap and attachments]

Thanks,
Alex Soto
Head of Ops, Elara Systems
alex.soto@elara.io

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@elara.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:20:47 -0700
Subject: Re: ServiceOps access audit & temporary break-glass request

Alex — great, thanks for the quick clarifications. Responding inline to your questions and confirming what Redwood can commit to in the MAP: 

1) Audit log granularity: we capture action verb + resource id + full request hash and metadata (actor id, timestamp, session id). By default we do not store full PII-bearing request/response bodies in plain text; instead we store redaction markers plus hashed payloads. If your compliance team needs verbatim content we can support encrypted session transcripts retained under a separate KMS wrapper for a defined retention period (this is an account-level option).

2) Break-glass approvals: we support a configurable approval policy. Proposed default for Elara: customer-initiated request via portal -> two customer approvers OR one customer approver + Redwood on-call (4-eyes) for high severity. All approvals trigger email + webhook notifications to your security channel. We can also push an event into your Slack channel on request.

Action items I will take this afternoon:
- Update privilege_matrix_draft.xlsx with two alternate profiles: 1) Scoped support (read-only + sanitized traces) and 2) Elevated on-call (timeboxed full session with encrypted transcript).
- Open HubSpot ticket and link it to the MAP (link below).

HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood.ai/contacts/ELR-2027-139
Drive (priv matrix): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B1Elara-ServiceOps

Attachments: privilege_matrix_draft_v2.xlsx (will be uploaded by EOD).

If Elara is fine with the two-profile approach, Marissa will schedule the SSO/SCIM PoC next week and we'll push the MAP to DocuSign.

Thanks — looping Marissa to pick PoC slots.

--
Karthik

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:30:05 -0700
Subject: RE: ServiceOps access audit & temporary break-glass request (internal)

Team — a few notes for MAP language and our proposal to Elara (internal only):

- Break-glass wording: propose we state "Temporary elevated access will be timeboxed (max 4 hours) and require explicit customer approval; all actions will be recorded and stored under the account's configured KMS policy." That gives legal a clear scope.
- Logging SLA: commit to 365-day retention for audit metadata; transcripts are an add-on in the MAP with separate KMS key.
- Residency: mark account as US-only (us-east) and make sure any backup snapshots are also restricted; add an acceptance checkbox in the onboarding flow.

Marissa — please confirm if you want us to push the DocuSign MAP with the SOC 2 clause included or keep that as a separate rider. I think including the clause will speed approvals.

Hannah
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@elara.io>, Elara Systems - Ops Team <elara-ops@elara.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: SSO PoC slots + MAP and DocuSign

Alex — thanks again. Quick next steps and asks so we can hit your target for budget approval next Tuesday: 

1) Please confirm two 1-hour windows for an SSO/SCIM PoC next week (we propose Tue 14 Jun 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 15 Jun 14:00-15:00 PT).
2) Confirm that Elara accepts the two-profile privilege model (Scoped support / Elevated on-call). If yes, we will finalize the privilege matrix and attach to the MAP.
3) Confirm that production residency is US (us-east) and that audit logs retention will be 365 days.

Deliverables Redwood will provide on signing:
- Final privilege matrix (v2) and break-glass SOP.
- DocuSign MAP with SOC 2 wording and an option to add encrypted transcript retention under a separate KMS.
- Support portal configuration to surface JIT requests + webhook to your security channel.

DocuSign MAP: https://www.docusign.com/ELR-2027-MAP
HubSpot ticket: https://hubspot.redwood.ai/contacts/ELR-2027-139
Drive (priv matrix v2): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B1Elara-ServiceOps

Attachments: redwood_scope_v1.pdf, privilege_matrix_draft_v2.xlsx

If those two PoC times don't work, send two alternatives and we'll lock the slot. Once PoC is done we can have the MAP signed quickly.

Best,
Marissa Cole
